key_insight: Plasma APOE4 proteotyping can closely match DNA APOE genotyping for identifying APOE ε4 carrier status and copy number, with similar Alzheimer’s disease associations.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this blood-based approach could offer a scalable alternative to genetic testing for risk stratification and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease research and care settings.
method: Measured plasma APOE4 using the NULISAseq CNS panel in four cohorts.
Used DNA-based APOE genotyping as the reference standard.
Compared genotype- vs proteotype-defined groups for amyloid positivity, CDR global score, and time to CDR-SB worsening.
evidence_signal: APOE4 proteotyping showed excellent classification performance in ADRC (AUC 0.977) and perfect external validation in three cohorts (AUC 1.000), with similar effect estimates to genotyping for key AD outcomes.
watch_item: The thresholds were derived in one cohort and should be independently validated across broader, more diverse populations before routine implementation.
paper_title: Clinical utility of plasma APOE proteotyping for Alzheimer's disease risk and prognosis
